text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnian sources claim the Tudjman-Izetbegovic meeting will be held in Zagreb on June 23.
- The government writes a letter to UN Security Council asking for the termination of the UNTAES mandate in its current form on July 15.
- Presidential candidate Vlado Gotovac pledges in a television interview he would create a state meeting all the needs of its people.
- Ericsson Nikola Tesla signs an agreement with Italian company Novotec on selling its tool-producing division.
- The US Bechtel construction company which has been chosen to build the Zagreb-Split motorway is to engage the strongest Turkish construction firm ENKA Holding Investment Co. as a collaborator.
- There is no need to fear Friday 13, as contrary to popular belief and according to Zagreb statistics catastrophes rarely happen on that day.
- I shall continue waging the politics I used to create a strong Croatia, says President Franjo Tudjman in an interview.
- A fire in Rijeka city hall stalled the election process for the region's prefect, but it later resumed and HDZ took over. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
